# v0.10.0 beta - C++ renderer

This beta release replaces the Python enhanced renderer with a C++ renderer,
with approximately **3-4x the performance of the Python renderer when
tested on a high-end CPU/GPU**.

It retains the loading-performance fix from v0.9.2, including the fix for
systems that fell to around 200 DOSBox cycles during mission loading.

## Changes since v0.9.2

- C++ renderer with full scene rendering, HUD, all weapon effects, view modes,
  and HUD damage effects.
- Direct `MW2.PRJ` resource loading, with a prominent diagnostic and
  guest-memory fallback if the archive cannot be loaded.
- Mission frame pacing now also applies to the original DOS renderer view
  and side-by-side presentation, in addition to the enhanced renderer view.
- Improved resource and OpenGL-context cleanup.
- Configuration startup failures now leave visible error output for reporting.
- Included dependency notices and matching renderer and FreeType source
  in the source bundle. Matching DOSBox-X source is available separately
  from [the v0.3.0 source snapshot](https://github.com/furious-pixel/dosbox-x-mod/archive/refs/tags/v0.3.0.zip).
- A smaller bundled Python runtime: Python remains for joystick input,
  gameplay fixes and configuration; NumPy, Numba and the Python OpenGL
  renderer are no longer needed.

**Supported platform:** Windows x64 on Intel or AMD 64-bit hardware.

## Installation and upgrade

Extract into a fresh directory. To migrate settings, copy only
`mw2mods/mod.conf` and, if present, `mw2mods/joystick.conf` from the previous
installation. Do not copy its Python environment or renderer files. Add your
own game files to the empty `game/` directory as described in README.md.

Keep v0.9.2 available as a fallback while evaluating this first native beta.
The package includes the matching native-capable DOSBox-X build; older
Python-only host builds are incompatible with the native renderer.

Source packaging simplified: the source bundle contains renderer and FreeType
source; DOSBox-X source is linked separately. Binary downloads are unchanged.
